newsitem.title: USA: Calif. business, voters optimistic on economy - poll.
newsitem.headline: Calif. business, voters optimistic on economy - poll.

text.p: California business leaders and voters are increasingly optimistic about the state's economic recovery, according to a survey released on Tuesday.

The non-partisan California Business Roundtable's survey found an 11 point rise in voters who expect the state's job opportunities to grow next year and a six point increase in voters who expect to be better off financially next year.
Seventy-three percent of voters expect to be living in the state five years from now, the survey found.

"This is very encouraging news for California, which has made great strides in repositioning itself as a business-friendly state," said John Bryson, chairman and chief executive officer at Edison International, and chairman of the California Business Roundtable.
Following is a sampling of the survey results and findings:
- 48 percent of business leaders plan to expand their California workforce in 1997.
- 83 percent of voters said that public education should be given the highest priority for state spending.
- A majority of respondents said they favor a school vouchers program.

- Improvements in infrastructure are needed most in the area of water supply, telecommunications and information systems, school construction and highways, roads and streets, according to business leaders.
- 55 percent of voters believe the initiative process is good for California.
The seventh annual California Business Roundtable survey was conducted in September and October.
The random telephone survey of 600 registered voters has a margin of error of plus or minus 4 percent.
The random sample mail survey of top officials from California companies includes 608 responses and also has a margin of error of plus or minus 4 percent.
